canonical_topic: Marginal supply sensitivity of power prices
definition: Because the generation stack is steep near the margin, even small changes in available supply can shift which unit is marginal and cause disproportionately large price moves.
core_idea: A relatively small quantity of added or removed supply near the top of the stack can move the market clearing price by a large amount, since the marginal generators being displaced set the price for the whole market.
key_points: During August 2005 in PJM, power prices were around $80/MWh.
A supply change of about 4,000 MWh was shown to move power prices by $10 or more (Figure 4.2.6), illustrating the steepness of the stack near the marginal generators active at that time.
relationships: Directly follows from variable generation shifting the top of the generation stack.
trading_implications: Small, seemingly minor changes in supply (e.g., from variable generation) can be a major driver of intraday price volatility.
